title: IN Operator
description: Learn how to use the IN operator to check whether a value matches any value in a list or a subquery.

data.alt: SQL Server IN with subquery example

data.text: The IN operator is a logical operator that allows you to check whether a value matches any value in a list.

data.title: IN Syntax
data.content: Check if a value matches any value in a list.

items: Specify the column or expression to test.
Specify a list of values to test. All values must have the same type as the column or expression.

data.text: If a value in the column or expression is equal to any value in the list, the result of the IN operator is TRUE.
The IN operator is equivalent to multiple OR operators:

data.title: IN vs OR Equivalence
data.content: IN is shorthand for multiple OR conditions.
data.code:
column IN (v1, v2, v3)

column = v1 OR column = v2 OR column = v3

data.text: To negate the IN operator, use the NOT IN operator:

data.title: NOT IN Syntax
data.content: NOT IN returns TRUE if the value does not match any value in the list.
data.code: column | expression NOT IN (v1, v2, v3, ...)

data.text: In addition to a list of values, you can use a subquery that returns a list of values with the IN operator:

data.title: IN with Subquery Syntax
data.content: Use a subquery to provide the list of values.

data.title: NULL in IN
data.text: If a list contains NULL, the result of IN or NOT IN will be UNKNOWN.

data.title: Basic IN Example
data.content: Find products with list price of 89.99, 109.99, or 159.99.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price IN (89.99, 109.99, 159.99)
ORDER BY
    list_price;

data.title: NOT IN Example
data.content: Find products without those specific prices.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price NOT IN (89.99, 109.99, 159.99)
ORDER BY
    list_price;

data.title: Subquery for Product IDs
data.content: Returns product IDs in stock at store 1 with quantity >= 30.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id
FROM
    production.stocks
WHERE
    store_id = 1 AND quantity >= 30;

data.title: IN with Subquery in WHERE Clause
data.content: Use the subquery above to filter products by matching product IDs.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    product_id IN (
        SELECT
            product_id
        FROM
            production.stocks
        WHERE
            store_id = 1 AND quantity >= 30
    )
ORDER BY
    product_name;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The IN operator checks if a value matches any value in a list or subquery.
IN is equivalent to multiple OR conditions but more concise.
Use NOT IN to find values that don't match any in the list.
IN can use a subquery to dynamically provide the list of values.
If the list contains NULL, IN and NOT IN may return UNKNOWN.
